statusText: Green - weekend halt across every published hour, Tail at its structural floor
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits far below the block threshold and no evidence-based danger window applies, because all twenty-four published hours fall inside the CME weekend halt and no price path can form. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active as always. The Sunday 22:00Z reopen falls beyond this window.
headline: A 3.75%-4.00% policy rate, a 10-year at the 5% threshold and $100 crude sit out the weekend halt behind a 14.81 VIX, with Tail at its floor
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt: cash trading ended at 20:00Z on Friday, the E-mini stopped printing near 21:00Z, and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, about fourteen hours after the final slot in this window. Friday's verified marks stand unchanged. Cash Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing within four points of the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range. VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and settled at the low of a 14.80-15.63 daily range. Friday was a quadruple-witching expiry alongside the quarterly index rebalance, among the largest such sessions on record, and it cleared without disorder; the closing strength was substantially mechanical flow rather than persistent momentum, which is why it is not read as one-way structure. The week's anchor was Wednesday's FOMC decision: a unanimous 12-0 vote raising the target range 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00%, the first increase in more than three years, with a dot plot pointing to at least one further hike this year. Equities absorbed it and then rose into rising long-end yields rather than falling ones; the 10-year closed Friday near the 5% threshold, up about five basis points, while H.15 for 17 September shows the 2-year at 4.67% and the 10-year at 4.94%. Energy eased, with WTI settling at $100.30, down about 1.6%, and Brent at $103.87, a third consecutive decline as the feared supply shock was reassessed downward. Reporting of an Iran-Oman plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remains unconfirmed by Omani officials, so partial de-escalation is treated as reducing conviction rather than as settled, and Hormuz shipping risk stays an unresolved discontinuity. Friday's internals were dispersed rather than aligned: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 2.78% on memory names while capital rotated out of mega-cap technology, and over the week the Nasdaq gained about 0.4% while the S&P 500 and the Dow posted losses, the Dow shedding more than 1.5%. The AI policy file is the newest amplifier candidate, with chip stocks recovering Friday after calls from AI developers for a slowdown and with AI chips and export controls on the agenda of the 24 September Trump-Xi meeting in Washington; both sit beyond this window. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was stale and only partially collected this cycle, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, so no part of this assessment rests on it and every figure here was verified independently against primary sources. Tail is held at its structural weekend floor because the pathological no-retracement structure it measures has no venue in which to develop. Stress is low and drifts higher only as the stock of unpriced headlines grows against static marks, and Confidence decays as Friday's evidence ages. The genuine sensitivity of this assessment sits beyond its final hour, at the Sunday reopen.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail ran 15-18 through the European morning and the dispersed U.S. cash session, then fell to 11, 7, 6 and 5 as trading ended and the contract settled, holding 5 across the final nine hours. Stress peaked at 51 during the U.S. afternoon and decayed through 44, 33, 28 and 26 into the halt, reaching 21 across the final four slots. Confidence held between 78 and 88 throughout, drifting lower only once the halt removed any refreshing observation. Dominant mode rotated from trend-up in the European morning to mixed across the dispersed U.S. session, back briefly to trend-up into the close, then to normal for every hour of the weekend halt.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed at 20:00Z on Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, about fourteen hours after the final slot here. Tail is held between 5 and 7 across the window, with a gradual lift through Saturday evening and the Sunday small hours that reflects the growing stock of unpriced headlines - principally the Hormuz supply file, the rates file after a hike that left the 10-year at the 5% threshold, and AI policy into the 24 September Trump-Xi meeting - rather than any observed structure. Stress rises slowly from 21 to 30 on the same reasoning, crossing into the moderate band during Saturday afternoon in New York, and Confidence decays from 77 to 66 as Friday's verified marks age without a refreshing observation. Dominant mode is normal in every slot and the mapped policy state is unchanged throughout. The genuine sensitivity of this assessment sits beyond its final hour, at the reopen, where a gap that extends without a meaningful retracement alongside aligned yields, crude and semiconductors would be the structure that matters; a gap that is absorbed and retraced would be ordinary.
